sources_considered.why: Readable reporting identifying a dismissed writer, the dismissal date, and the replacement publishing process.
Readable transcript of Duolingo's CEO acknowledging AI-related contractor reductions.
Read as a cross-check; the CEO's subsequent explanation provides more direct evidence and preserves the contractor-versus-employee distinction.
Read relevant passages. Artist layoffs and compulsory AI use do not by themselves establish that AI caused those layoffs.

evidence_items.locator: Second article paragraph, quoting former writer Matías S. Zavia
evidence_items.explanation: The report documents dismissal of the Spanish editorial staff and replacement with automated translations. It supplies a completed editorial substitution; no direct employer announcement was obtained.

evidence_items.publisher: Duolingo; earnings-call transcript hosted by Reportify
evidence_items.locator: Q4 2023 earnings call, Luis von Ahn's response about contractor reductions and AI
evidence_items.explanation: On this date the CEO confirmed completed contractor reductions and identified AI as their main probable cause. He described translation and content work and explicitly distinguished these reductions from full-time employee layoffs.

unresolved_gaps: These cases do not measure how common replacement is across companies.
The evidence does not independently establish replacement in every named occupation or management's emotional enthusiasm.
